title: feat(console): the login page takes one primary hue, a leaner card, a quiet dev-admin row and a footer (objectui#12600)
body:
Fixes #12600
Clause-②: yes

The console login page follows the approved artboard "登录页 · A 精修居中版": one accent hue, a leaner card that carries its own header, a quiet dev-admin row in place of the amber banner, and a footer with the locale switch and the legal links the server serves.

This PR resumes a run that ended mid-build (the earlier session ran out of tokens after pushing four commits, with no PR and no report). Every inherited commit was re-read hunk by hunk against the card's Target, Acceptance and Constraints; every verification below was re-run on this branch.

## What changes

- **One accent** (`apps/console/src/pages/auth/AuthLayout.tsx`). The brand tile is `bg-primary` and the glow is `bg-primary/10` in both themes; no `indigo-*` class remains. The dot grid moves from an inline `style` to Tailwind arbitrary utilities. The shell root gains `isolate`: the `-z-10` depth layer used to paint beneath the root's own `bg-background`, so neither the dot grid nor the glow ever showed on any auth page. A new `formWidth: 'base'` gives the 400 px column.
- **The card** (`apps/console/src/pages/auth/LoginPage.tsx`). `rounded-xl`, 1 px border, `px-7 pt-7 pb-5`. Its own header, "Welcome back" (`text-xl font-semibold`) and one 13 px muted line, "Sign in to continue your work". `LoginForm` renders with the new `hideHeader`, so the lock tile and the two-line header are gone.
- **`LoginForm`** (`packages/auth/src/LoginForm.tsx`). An optional `hideHeader` prop (default `false`: header unchanged), with the SSO-only description kept as one muted line under SSO-only mode. A 28 px password show/hide toggle, its accessible names taken from two new optional labels, `showPasswordText` / `hidePasswordText`. The root caps its width with `sm:max-w-[400px]` instead of fixing it with `sm:w-[400px]`. The enterprise SSO button is 40 px with the inputs' radius. The "Sign up" line is 13 px and still renders only when the host passes `registerUrl`, which the console passes only when `decideSignUpOffer` answers `form`.
- **Shared auth styles** (`packages/auth/src/authStyles.tsx`). Inputs and the primary button are 40 px (`h-10`, were `h-11`). The button is one flat `bg-primary` fill (was a `--primary` gradient). Field labels are 13 px.
- **Dev instance.** The amber banner, which printed the seed password, is gone. The card's last row, under a dashed top border, reads "Local development instance" and carries a 28 px outline chip, "Sign in as dev admin", that calls the same `useAuth().signIn` the form calls with the email and password `/auth/config` reported. The password is never rendered. The row exists only when `/auth/config` reports `devSeedAdmin`. A seed reported without a password shows the email and no chip.
- **Footer.** The existing `LocaleSwitcher` at the left. At the right, "Privacy" and "Terms" links, each only when the server's auth config serves `features.privacyUrl` / `features.termsUrl`. A URL that is neither `http(s)` nor a same-origin path renders no link.
- **`DefaultLoginPage`** (`packages/app-shell/src/console/auth/LoginPage.tsx`) passes the translated names of the new toggle. It keeps its split-panel layout and the form's own header.
- **i18n**, all ten packs. Added `auth.login.welcomeTitle`, `welcomeDescription`, `showPasswordText`, `hidePasswordText`, `footer.privacy`, `footer.terms`, `devAdminHint.signIn`. `devAdminHint.title` now reads "Local development instance". Removed `devAdminHint.body` and `devAdminHint.dismiss`: they named the retired banner's credentials line and dismiss button, and `check:i18n-dead-keys` listed both as confirmed dead on the inherited tip.

Unchanged, per the card's constraints: `?redirect=`, the SSO hand-off, the server-unreachable panel (it gets the same `max-w` treatment, so it fits the narrower card), the server-driven product name and logo, and the sign-up rule.

## The inherited commits, judged

| Commit | Content | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `6a585d1` | feature: AuthLayout, console LoginPage, LoginForm, authStyles, DefaultLoginPage labels, locales | kept; two dead locale keys removed in `8065049` |
| `a723731` | tests: layout, header opt-out, toggle, dev row | kept; extended in `8065049` |
| `42ed089` | four changesets | console, auth and app-shell kept; the i18n one rewritten in `8065049` to name the two removals |
| `9603dd3` | i18n residue anchor reads the new en label | kept |

`8e22590` merges `origin/main` at `63d00da` (no file on this surface changed on main since the branch base).

## Measurements against the dispatch's hypotheses

- **H1, `LoginFormProps`.** Built `@object-ui/auth` twice, once with the merge-base versions of `LoginForm.tsx` and `authStyles.tsx` restored under a trap and once at HEAD. The diff of `dist/LoginForm.d.ts`: `LoginFormProps` gains exactly `hideHeader?: boolean`, and `LoginFormLabels` gains exactly `showPasswordText?: string` and `hidePasswordText?: string`. Nothing is removed or renamed, and no existing default moved in the source. `dist/authStyles.d.ts`: the three class constants are declared with their literal values, so their declared types change with the values (`h-11` to `h-10`, gradient to flat, 13 px label).
- **H2, changesets.** Four `minor` changesets: console, auth, app-shell, i18n. No `major`. Each one's wording was checked against the diff; only the i18n one needed a change.
- **H3, dev-admin row.** Pinned in `LoginPage.dev-admin-hint.test.tsx`: the row only with `devSeedAdmin`; the password string absent from the whole document's markup; the chip calling the client's `signIn` with the reported credentials; and, new in this PR, the chip landing where a typed sign-in lands (the console root, `RootLandingRedirect`'s door to home), honouring a safe `?redirect=`, and replaying the authorize request under an SSO hand-off. Ablations below.
- **H4, footer config.** `features.termsUrl` / `features.privacyUrl` are real keys: the spec lists them in `PUBLIC_AUTH_CONFIG_NON_FLAG_KEYS`, and objectstack's auth manager serves them (it defaults them to its own public pages, and an empty `OS_TERMS_URL` / `OS_PRIVACY_URL` omits them). For the version/environment pill, the config the preview badge reads (`AppShellRuntimeConfig` in `packages/app-shell/src/runtime-config.ts`, produced by objectstack's `RuntimeConfigPlugin`) carries `branding.stage` and no product version or environment label. The only `environment` there is `telemetry.clientErrorReporting.environment`, an error-reporting tag present only with a DSN. So no pill is drawn and no key is invented.
- **H5, `DefaultLoginPage`.** Needed. The toggle lives in `LoginForm`, so `DefaultLoginPage` renders it too, and without the two labels its accessible names stay English in every locale.
- **H6, unchanged behaviour.** `?redirect=`: `authExitBasename.test.tsx`, "LoginPage — redirect behaviour is unchanged by the lift". Server unreachable: `LoginPage.server-unreachable-11806.test.tsx`. SSO callback error: `LoginPage.error-banner.test.tsx`. No test pinned the SSO hand-off before this PR. `LoginPage.dev-admin-hint.test.tsx` now pins it for both a typed sign-in and the chip: the "Continue to" banner, and `followOauthAuthorize` called with the page's query string instead of a navigation.

## Tests and gates (run at `8065049`)

All runs below are at `8065049`, from the worktree root, through the shared verify lock.

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/auth/ packages/app-shell/src/console/auth/ packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/product-neutral-renderer.ratchet.test.ts apps/console/src/pages/auth/ apps/console/src/__tests__/i18nAfterSignIn-12034.test.tsx`: `Test Files  57 passed (57)`, `Tests  477 passed (477)`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/i18n/`: `Test Files  83 passed (83)`, `Tests  1321 passed | 13 skipped (1334)`. The 13 skips are the `describe.runIf(DRIVEN)` time-zone legs of `formatting.dateOnlyZone-10866.test.ts`, which this diff does not touch.
- Declared narrowing: the full `packages/app-shell/` suite (1435 test files) and the full `apps/console/` suite were not run locally; CI runs both. The app-shell diff is two label lines in `DefaultLoginPage`, whose tests are all under `packages/app-shell/src/console/auth/`. Outside `pages/auth/`, the one console test that renders the real `LoginPage` is `i18nAfterSignIn-12034.test.tsx` (run above). The other App-level tests stub it.
- Type-check, after `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/console^...' build` (35 packages, exit 0): `pnpm --filter @object-ui/auth type-check`, `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/console`, each echoing `tsc --noEmit` plus its test project and each exiting 0. The console passes `hideHeader` and the two new labels, and the pre-change declaration refuses all three. So a green console type-check can only have read the rebuilt `.d.ts`.
- `pnpm check:i18n-keys`, `pnpm check:i18n-drift`, `pnpm check:i18n-dead-keys`: exit 0 each. Drift: "Every changed en value was followed by all nine translation packs." Dead keys: no `auth.login` entry remains (the inherited tip listed `devAdminHint.body` and `devAdminHint.dismiss` as confirmed).
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims`, `pnpm changeset:check`, `pnpm check:test-path-roots`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`), `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0 each.
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` over the 19 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files: 0 errors and 4 warnings. All four sit on lines this diff does not change: two `set-state-in-effect`, one `exhaustive-deps` whose disable comment `--no-inline-config` ignores, and one unused `hasSocialProviders`.
- Control-byte scan over every changed file: no hits.

## Ablations

Each mutation went through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor must hit, the blob must change, then restore proven by blob hash against HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`). Tests import the packages' sources through the vitest aliases, so no build sits between the mutation and the run.

| Mutation | Pins that went red | Restore |
|---|---|---|
| password into the chip's `title` attribute | "never puts the password in the DOM", "renders the row and its sign-in chip", "says why a refused sign-in failed" (3 of 10) | blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty |
| row rendered without `devSeedAdmin` | "renders no row without devSeedAdmin" (1 of 10) | same |
| chip's `signIn` call replaced by a no-op | "signs in with the reported email and password", "says why a refused sign-in failed", "lands where a typed sign-in lands", "honours a safe ?redirect=", "the chip under an SSO hand-off" (5 of 10) | same |
| `LoginForm` ignores `hideHeader` | auth "renders no header when the host opts out", "still says how to sign in under SSO-only mode", console "draws one header, its own" (3 of 14) | same |
| brand tile back to `bg-indigo-500` | "names no indigo class in its source", "draws the brand tile and the glow from --primary" (2 of 8) | same |

Every ablation went red, as predicted. The first spelling of the password ablation (a hidden span appended after the chip's label) kept its anchor inside the replacement, so `ablation-replace` refused it as a mutation that moved no anchor and ran no test. It was re-run with the attribute spelling above.

## NOT MEASURED

- NOT MEASURED: screenshots, reason: the seat takes one shared browser reading for the resumed cards at review, before ACCEPT. The card's acceptance item 2 (1280 px, light and dark, with and without `devSeedAdmin`) is carried by the `domain:ui` seat.

## Acceptance notes

Where the delivered page differs from the artboard's numbers. Each item is noted here and not filed.

1. **No version/environment pill** (Target 7). The runtime config the preview badge reads has no product version or display environment (see H4). Drawing one would need a new runtime-config key, a contract change outside this card. Carrier: none.
2. **The locale switch is the existing icon-only `LocaleSwitcher`** (a 32 px globe button with a menu), not "🌐 简体中文 ▾" with a label and caret. The card names the existing component. A labelled variant would change app-shell's published `LocaleSwitcher`, which is outside the declared file surface. Carrier: none.
3. **Radii are theme tokens, not the artboard's pixels.** This console sets `--radius: 0.875rem` (the iOS-scale `@layer base` block in `apps/console/src/index.css`) and `--radius-xl: 1rem`. So `rounded-lg` (fields, button, chip) computes to 14 px rather than 8 px, and the card's `rounded-xl` to 16 px rather than 12 px. The inherited code kept the theme radii under the constraint "Tailwind utilities and theme tokens only". The seat's browser reading is where this gets judged. Carrier: the `domain:ui` seat's review reading.
4. **Provider buttons and their divider** live in `SocialSignInButtons`, outside the declared surface. The buttons are 40 px but `rounded-md` (12 px here, not 8 px). The divider label paints on `bg-background`, and on this card that is not `--card` (light: `240 24% 97%` against white). The label would sit on a visible patch whenever a provider is configured. This is read from source and not reproduced in a browser in this run, so it is not filed. Carrier: the seat's browser reading with a provider configured.
5. **zh divider wording** stays "或使用邮箱继续" (the artboard reads "或使用邮箱"). The key's wording matches the register page's, and both are pinned by the existing social-label locale tests. Carrier: none.
6. **Types.** `AuthPublicConfig.features` in `@object-ui/auth` declares the spec's `tenancyPosture` and `audiencePosture` but not the other two `PUBLIC_AUTH_CONFIG_NON_FLAG_KEYS`, `termsUrl` and `privacyUrl`, so the page reads them through a narrowing cast (as it already did for `devSeedAdmin`). Declaring them is a published-type change in `packages/auth/src/types.ts`, outside the declared surface. Carrier: none.
7. **Docs.** `packages/auth/README.md` documents `labels` in general and lists no `LoginForm` prop (not even `hideIcon`), and `content/docs` has no `LoginForm` page. So there is no prop list for `hideHeader` to join.
8. A browser that dismissed the old banner keeps an `os.console.devAdminHintDismissed` entry in `localStorage`. Nothing reads it any more, and it is harmless.
